reason: The cited evidence does not address FeNiCrMn or the twinning–slip transition. E1 concerns a dual-phase AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy and adiabatic shear bands, E2 describes jerky flow and slip avalanches in HEAs, and E3 compares CrCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi without discussing twinning mechanisms. None of the key premises are supported by the cited passages.
premises: Deformation twinning and dislocation slip are the competing mechanisms in FeNiCrMn
Low temperature and high strain rate suppress dislocation mobility and promote twinning
High twin density enhances strain hardening and preserves strength–ductility balance
Higher temperature or lower strain rate favours dislocation glide and recovery with minimal twinning
The mechanism transition is supported by prior evidence on related high/medium-entropy alloys
